html:
Elderly Home Care in Tashkent

Caring for aging parents, grandparents, or other elderly relatives is an important responsibility. However, work, children, household responsibilities, and everyday life do not always make it possible to stay with an elderly family member throughout the entire day.

The situation can become more challenging when an elderly person has limited mobility, is bedridden, or needs assistance with personal hygiene, eating, moving around, and other daily activities.

In such situations, elderly home care can provide practical daytime support while allowing the person to remain in the familiar environment of their own home.

Through Onlayn Hamshira, families in Tashkent can arrange an 8-hour daily home care service for elderly and bedridden patients. The service can be booked for one day or for several consecutive days.

Important: Home care is intended for daily support and assistance. It does not replace medical examination, diagnosis, treatment, or hospital care.

What is elderly home care?

Elderly home care is more than simply having someone stay beside an older person. It involves practical assistance with everyday activities that may have become difficult because of age, reduced mobility, recovery after treatment, or another condition.

An elderly person may need help with bathing, changing clothes, eating, moving safely, maintaining personal hygiene, or other daily routines.

Some patients may also become temporarily or permanently bedridden after surgery, an injury, a stroke, or another medical condition.

Family members often try to provide all of this care themselves. However, daily caregiving can require considerable time, physical effort, patience, and attention.

Professional home care can help families share these responsibilities while allowing the elderly person to remain at home.

Who may need elderly home care?

Home care can be useful in many different situations.

An elderly parent may still live independently but require assistance with certain activities during the day. Other patients may need more extensive support because they have limited mobility or spend most of their time in bed.

Home care may be suitable for:

  • elderly people with reduced mobility;
  • bedridden patients;
  • elderly patients recovering after surgery or treatment;
  • people who cannot manage personal hygiene independently;
  • patients who need assistance during meals;
  • families requiring temporary daytime care;
  • elderly parents who need support while their children are at work.

The exact level of assistance depends on the person's condition, mobility, daily routine, and individual needs.

How does the 8-hour daily care service work?

Through Onlayn Hamshira, elderly home care can be arranged in an 8-hour daily format.

This can be convenient for families whose members leave for work in the morning and return home later in the day.

A specialist comes to the patient's home and provides agreed daily assistance during the care period.

The service does not have to be limited to one day. If additional support is required, families can request care for several consecutive days.

This may be useful when relatives are traveling, working, managing other family responsibilities, or when an elderly person temporarily needs additional support after treatment.

What can elderly home care include?

The exact range of tasks depends on the patient's condition and the requirements agreed before the service begins.

Daily care for bedridden patients

A bedridden patient may be unable to manage many everyday activities independently. A care specialist can assist with routine needs and help the patient remain as comfortable as possible during the day.

For patients who spend long periods in bed, daily assistance may include hygiene, meals, changing position, and other agreed care tasks.

Bathing and personal hygiene

Personal hygiene is an important part of elderly and bedridden patient care.

Depending on the patient's mobility and condition, assistance may include bathing, body hygiene, changing clothes, and maintaining a clean and comfortable environment.

Nail care

Simple tasks such as trimming nails can become difficult for an older person with limited mobility.

When included in the care plan, a specialist can assist with basic nail care and other routine personal-care activities.

Repositioning in bed

Remaining in the same position for a long time can cause discomfort for a bedridden patient.

Carefully changing the patient's position may therefore be part of daily support. The patient's medical condition, mobility restrictions, and physician recommendations should always be taken into account.

Assistance with meals

Some elderly people can eat independently but need food prepared and placed within reach. Others may require direct assistance during meals.

If a physician has prescribed a special diet or eating schedule, those instructions should be followed.

Can injections and IV infusions be provided?

If a patient requires injections or intravenous infusions during the care period, these procedures should only be performed by an appropriately qualified healthcare professional and according to a physician's prescription or medical instruction.

A caregiver does not independently prescribe medication, select treatment, or change a patient's treatment plan.

If medication or a medical procedure has been prescribed, the physician's instructions should clearly specify the medication, dosage, method of administration, and treatment schedule.

Home care does not replace medical treatment or physician supervision.

Why is home care convenient for elderly people?

Many elderly people are accustomed to their own home, room, daily routine, and familiar surroundings.

Moving to an unfamiliar environment can be stressful or uncomfortable, particularly for a person with reduced mobility or health-related limitations.

Home care allows an elderly person to remain in familiar surroundings while receiving the daily assistance they need.

This arrangement can also be more practical for the family. Relatives can continue visiting and spending time with their loved one while sharing some of the daily caregiving responsibilities with a professional.

In a large city such as Tashkent, balancing work, commuting, family responsibilities, and several hours of daily caregiving can be difficult.

Professional assistance can help distribute those responsibilities more realistically.

What should families consider when choosing a caregiver?

Entrusting an elderly family member to another person is an important decision. Price should not be the only consideration.

The specialist's experience, responsibility, communication style, patience, and careful approach to the patient are also important.

Professionals working with elderly people should be respectful, attentive, and patient, especially when assisting with bathing, changing clothes, repositioning a bedridden patient, or other personal-care activities.

Through the Onlayn Hamshira platform, families can request available home healthcare services according to their needs and location.

Is professional care only necessary for severely ill patients?

No.

Home care can also be useful for elderly people who can still walk and manage many activities independently.

For example, a person may only need help with bathing, dressing, eating, or certain daily routines.

Some families may also want a responsible professional to remain with their elderly parent during the hours when other family members are at work.

Daily care can therefore be useful even when an elderly person is not bedridden.

Should you book one day or several days?

That depends on the family's situation.

Sometimes care is required for only one day. For example, family members may have an important commitment, a trip, or another temporary responsibility.

In other cases, support may be needed for several consecutive days. This can happen after discharge from a hospital or during a temporary recovery period when an elderly person needs more assistance than usual.

With Onlayn Hamshira, families can request care for the period they actually need, subject to service availability.

How much does elderly home care cost?

The cost of home care can vary depending on the patient's condition, the amount of assistance required, and the scope of the requested service.

Caring for an elderly person who can walk independently is different from caring for a fully bedridden patient who requires extensive assistance with hygiene, meals, and positioning.

If prescribed medical procedures such as injections or IV infusions are also required, the service requirements may differ.

The most practical approach is to select the required service through the Onlayn Hamshira application and review the available conditions during the booking process.

What is the main benefit for adult children?

One of the main benefits of professional daytime care is the ability to distribute time and responsibility more effectively.

Caring for parents is important, but adult children may also need to work, support their own families, and manage other daily responsibilities.

Using professional home care does not mean abandoning responsibility for a parent. Instead, it can allow some physically demanding and repetitive daily tasks to be shared with a professional.

This may leave family members with more time and energy to spend with their loved one.

Sharing caregiving responsibilities can also make long-term family care more manageable.

How can you order elderly home care in Tashkent?

The service can be requested through the Onlayn Hamshira application.

When submitting a request, it is useful to provide clear information about the patient's condition and the type of assistance required.

For example:

  • Can the patient walk independently?
  • Is the patient bedridden?
  • Is help with bathing required?
  • Does the patient need assistance with meals?
  • Are there physician-prescribed injections or IV infusions?
  • How many hours and days is care required?

The more accurately the situation is described, the easier it is for the available specialist to understand the expected tasks.

If medical procedures are required, the physician's prescription or instructions should also be available.

How should the family prepare before the specialist arrives?

It is useful to prepare basic information about the patient in advance.

The specialist may need to know about the person's mobility, eating routine, allergies, medical restrictions, and physician recommendations.

If there are specific instructions for lifting or repositioning the patient, these should also be communicated before care begins.

Personal hygiene products, clean clothing, food, and other necessary items should ideally be kept nearby and easily accessible.

When should a doctor be contacted?

Home care does not replace medical assessment. If an elderly person's condition suddenly worsens, new concerning symptoms appear, or there is a medical emergency, the family should contact a doctor or emergency medical service as appropriate.

Caregivers should not independently diagnose a new condition, prescribe medication, or change an existing treatment plan.

Does elderly home care replace medical supervision?

No. Elderly home care focuses on everyday support and assistance. It does not replace medical examination, diagnosis, treatment, or physician supervision.

Can elderly home care be arranged for one day?

Yes. Families can request temporary elderly home care for one day, subject to service availability and the required care format.

Can elderly home care be arranged for several days?

Yes. Care can be requested for several consecutive days when additional daytime support is needed, subject to service availability.

Is home care suitable for bedridden patients?

It can be. Depending on the patient's condition and the available service, care may include assistance with hygiene, meals, repositioning, and other daily needs.

Can a caregiver give injections or IV infusions?

Medical procedures such as injections and IV infusions should only be performed by an appropriately qualified healthcare professional and according to a physician's prescription or medical instruction.

Onlayn Hamshira allows families in Tashkent to request available home healthcare services through the mobile application. Availability depends on the location and professionals available at the time of the request.
